_doc: Hardcoded FALLBACK thresholds — used ONLY if the backend has never sent 'config' in the /sensors/telemetry response, or if a field in 'config' is null. Once the backend sends valid config for a field, that remote value is used (see config/threshold_resolver.py). This JSON intentionally matches the API 'config' shape so fallback occurs per field, not all-or-nothing.
_smokeDangerThreshold_note: composite smokeLevel MQ-2+MQ-135 (0-100%), see _calc_smoke_level() in main.py.
_soilMoistureDangerThreshold_note: Soil moisture percentage. A value BELOW this threshold means dry/dangerous (lower_is_worse evaluation).
_humidityDangerThreshold_note: Air humidity percentage. A value BELOW this threshold means dry/dangerous (lower_is_worse evaluation).
_waterDangerThreshold_note: Water level (m) in the reservoir/tank. A value BELOW this threshold means the water is running low (lower_is_worse evaluation). The API example sends null for this field on some devices; when null, this local value is used.
_pressureDangerThreshold_note: Bar. This uses the same sensor as waterDangerThreshold, with a different unit (bar instead of meters). This local value is derived from waterDangerThreshold (0.5 m x 0.0980665 = ~0.049 bar) for consistency, but the backend may treat it as an independent threshold. It uses lower_is_worse evaluation (falling pressure means a lower water level). The API example sends null for this field; when null, this local value is used. The backend has not explicitly confirmed this value, so adjust it if the backend defines its own threshold.
_rainfallDangerThreshold_note: mm. Compared with rainfall_last_hour_mm (the sensor's one-hour window, NOT the delta since the last telemetry payload, because alarm evaluation runs much more often than telemetry transmission). Uses lower_is_worse=False: HIGH rainfall is dangerous, like high smoke, temperature, or wind. The value 1.0 matches a value previously sent by the backend and is used as fallback when this field is null.
_windDangerThreshold_note: m/s. There is no equivalent in the API response (the API does not send a wind threshold), so this field is ALWAYS local and is never overridden remotely.

alarm._note: The local siren (relay) only turns on after N readings of CONSECUTIVE have passed the danger threshold in a row. This is independent of emergency delivery uploads to the backend.
